justifications.c1: No per-incident loss for private estate stations is sourced. The £3k–£8k per room clean-up figure comes from a commercial cleaning blog. Water-company compensation (£150–£1,000) applies only to public sewers, and the EA fines (£2m, £330k, £300k) were against water companies, not private owners. The idea's £10k+ per home was not confirmed.
justifications.c2: Housing Ombudsman cases show repeat incidents at single stations (Walsall: blockages in February and July 2024 and continuing ingress, search-confirmed; Hexagon: overflows in October and December 2021). No failure-rate data or station count was found, and servicing is quarterly at most.
justifications.c3: Paid contracted servicing is documented with values: Wandle £302k over up to 4 years, a £200k–£550k 5-year contract, and Eastlight quarterly servicing across 50 sites. Local float alarms cost about £155. Costs per site are not broken out, and the sensor adds alerting rather than removing servicing.
justifications.c4: Owners are responsible for unadopted stations (Northumbrian, Thames, Anglian, Southern guidance), and the Housing Ombudsman makes maladministration findings. However, no rule requires monitoring or records for private stations, no private-station EA prosecution was found, and the 'monitoring mandated' source is US only.
justifications.c5: Housing associations evidently hold pump-maintenance budgets (tenders), and new-build estates use management companies funded by service charges (£600/yr, Frimley). No job title or role description with budget was found.
justifications.c6: Pump-station service contractors already sell monitoring for this exact site type: Southern Pump Services sells GSM dial-out telemetry and services housing-estate stations (search-confirmed), and CG Godfrey deploys Pow-Electrics IIoT kits. Water companies also offer monitoring to developers before adoption.
justifications.c7: The category is commoditised: GSM dial-out units, £155 float alarms, Permagard AlertMaxx2, Kingspan SmartServ Pro (£564 ex VAT) and water-company monitoring contracts. The gap is whether owners fit alarms, not a missing product, and no complaints about incumbents were found.
justifications.c8: Level-sensing modules and current clamps are standard. The wet well is a harsh environment, partly underground with RF problems, and its possible explosive atmosphere and ATEX zoning were not checked. No component prices were found apart from the £155 float alarm.
justifications.c9: Stations need ongoing operation, multi-year maintenance contracts exist, and a Middle Level 'Telemetry charges 576.00' line appears (period unknown). The Anglian £69/£86 monitoring price could not be confirmed in search, a different Anglian page shows a £889.10 monitoring contract with an unclear unit, and there is no statutory record schedule.
justifications.c10: Housing Ombudsman decisions (Settle, Walsall, Sovereign, Hexagon), a WATRS adjudication, local news (Surrey Live, Kent Online, Bognor, inkl/Cramlington), an MSE forum thread and EA enforcement releases. The regulator data concern water companies, not private estate stations.

weakest: Cheap GSM dial-out alarms and contractor telemetry already exist and are sold by the same pump-service contractors, and no private-estate loss figure or monitoring duty is sourced to justify a new product.
